name: Chapter 7: Integrals
description: Antiderivatives, substitution, trigonometric identities, standard forms, partial fractions, integration by parts, definite integrals, the fundamental theorems and properties, with every exercise verified.

cards.definition: The inverse process of differentiation: given f, find F with F′ = f. Then ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C
The constant of integration: F(x) + C is also an antiderivative for every constant C. So an indefinite integral is a family of curves, all vertical translates of one another

cards.term: When do you use partial fractions?
cards.definition: For a rational function P(x)/Q(x). If deg P ≥ deg Q, divide first (polynomial + proper fraction); then factor Q and split

(px + q)/((x − a)(x − b)): A/(x − a) + B/(x − b); (px + q)/(x − a)²: A/(x − a) + B/(x − a)²; (px² + qx + r)/((x − a)(x − b)(x − c)): A/(x − a) + B/(x − b) + C/(x − c); (px² + qx + r)/((x − a)²(x − b)): A/(x − a) + B/(x − a)² + C/(x − b); (px² + qx + r)/((x − a)(x² + bx + c)): A/(x − a) + (Bx + C)/(x² + bx + c)

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Properties of definite integrals

State the property.

P₁∫ₐᵇ f = −∫ᵦᵃ f; ∫ₐᵃ f = 0
P₂∫ₐᵇ f = ∫ₐᶜ f + ∫꜀ᵇ f (split at any c)
P₃∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x) dx (King)
P₄∫₀ᵃ f(x) dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a − x) dx
P₅∫₀^(2a) f(x) dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(x) dx + ∫₀ᵃ f(2a − x) dx
P₆∫₀^(2a) f = 2∫₀ᵃ f if f(2a − x) = f(x); = 0 if f(2a − x) = −f(x)
P₇∫_(−a)^(a) f = 2∫₀ᵃ f if f even; = 0 if f odd

P₃/P₄ are the “King property”; P₇ handles symmetric limits

cards.definition: Property P4: integral of f(x) from a to b equals integral of f(a+b-x); for f = sin x/(sin x+cos x) on [0,pi/2], f(x)+f(pi/2-x)=1 so I = pi/4

cards.term: Integrals of even and odd functions over [−a, a]

cards.term: How to use P₃ (King) in practice?
cards.definition: Call the integral I, replace x by a + b − x to get a second expression, add the two: if f(x) + f(a + b − x) is simple (often 1 or a constant), 2I = ∫(that) and I follows. Typical: ratios like sin/(sin + cos), log(1 + tan x)
